hero.subtitle: Losing someone in a Woodland traffic collision changes everything, and Yolo County families deserve clear answers, not more confusion. LawProactive connects you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death claims arising from crashes on roads like Main Street and I-5.

about.title: Woodland Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a traffic collision on E Main Street, East Street, I-5, or Main Street takes someone's life, the grief is compounded by practical burdens: funeral costs, lost income, and the sudden absence of a parent, spouse, or partner. Woodland recorded 2 traffic deaths alongside 157 injury collisions in the most recent full year, a reminder that even a community of under 60,000 people isn't immune to these losses. California law gives certain surviving family members a limited window and a specific path to hold a negligent driver accountable through a civil wrongful death claim. This is separate from any criminal proceeding and focuses on the financial and emotional toll on the family left behind. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we connect grieving families with an independent attorney who can evaluate the collision, identify who qualifies to bring the claim, and explain what compensation may be available under California statute.

items.title: Only Certain Relatives Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some situations. An independent attorney can clarify who in your family qualifies before any claim moves forward.

items.title: The Clock Starts Running Quickly
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity, such as a public roadway agency, may be involved. Waiting too long can close off options entirely.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs and lost financial support, but also the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a person provided. An attorney can help document both the financial and personal dimensions of the loss.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in Woodland?
items.answer: Under California law, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children generally have first priority to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify depending on the family's circumstances. An independent attorney can review your specific family situation to confirm standing.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to a criminal case?
items.answer: No. Even if the at-fault driver faces criminal charges related to a crash on a corridor like I-5 or Main Street, the wrongful death claim is a separate civil action pursued by the family. The two proceedings run independently and have different standards and outcomes.

items.question: How long do we have to act after a fatal crash in Yolo County?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file, though that period is shorter if a government agency is a potential defendant, which can matter given Woodland's mix of city streets and I-5 access points. It's wise to have an attorney review the timeline as early as possible.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything for this help?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and there's no cost to be matched with an independent attorney. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless a recovery is obtained.
